audit_findings.title: Terminal cash taxes may omit the Bermuda 15% regime
audit_findings.mechanism: Additional Bermuda cash taxes would reduce forecast and terminal owner earnings once the two-of-four-year revenue test is satisfied.
audit_findings.evidence: We will become subject to corporate income taxes in Bermuda once revenues exceed €750 million.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved modeling possibility, not a demonstrated omission: the record does not show scenario-specific threshold dates or taxable Bermuda constituent earnings. It is nevertheless material because the filed rate is 15% and terminal value supplies 47.7%-51.5% of scenario value, so an omitted terminal tax transition could meaningfully reduce the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Project consolidated revenue by scenario, apply the €750 million two-of-four-year test, identify taxable Bermuda constituent income and foreign-tax credits, and rerun owner earnings and terminal value with the resulting cash taxes.

audit_findings.title: Gross Amazon warrant dilution is unmatched by exercise proceeds
audit_findings.magnitude: $11.038 million omitted gross-exercise proceeds, equal to 4.2%-5.7% of scenario equity value and about $0.68 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: The valuation uses the 1.171812 million gross warrant shares in the denominator without adding the $9.42-per-share exercise proceeds to the equity bridge; net settlement would instead reduce dilution.
audit_findings.evidence: The warrant provides for net share settlement, that if elected by the holder, will reduce the number of shares issued upon exercise to reflect the net settlement of the exercise price.
audit_findings.explanation: The numerator-denominator inconsistency is demonstrated. Under the gross-exercise convention, correcting it adds approximately $0.68 per share; even the bull value would remain about $16.93 versus the $39.17 market price. The error therefore does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rerun with either gross warrant shares plus $11.038 million proceeds or contractually calculated net-settlement shares, and perform the same consistency check for employee options.

audit_findings.title: Safeguard creates potentially omitted claims ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.4 million filed maximum exposure to loss at March 31, 2026, equal to 1.3%-1.8% of scenario equity value; additional early-termination amounts unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Lease-guaranty, severance and asset-loss obligations could require cash not captured in recurring owner earnings or the debt-only bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s variable interest includes certain lease guaranty and exposure to certain severance payment obligations for Safeguard employees servicing ibex's account.
audit_findings.explanation: No omitted payable is demonstrated. The latest filing reports $3.4 million of maximum exposure but separately states that early-termination amounts cannot be reasonably estimated and considers loss remote. The quantified exposure alone is modest, while the record cannot establish the size or probability of the additional claims.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the Safeguard contract and schedules, separate recoverable assets from lease and severance guarantees, quantify termination scenarios and probabilities, review subsequent developments, and rerun the bridge with any expected-value liability.

audit_findings.title: The bridge may treat operating or restricted cash as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $15.409 million added to the bridge; $2.2 million was restricted and $9.4 million was outside the United States; full removal equals about $0.95 per share and 5.9%-7.9% of scenario equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required for working capital, restricted from distribution or subject to repatriation costs should be excluded or haircut in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of June 30, 2025, we had cash and cash equivalents of $15.4 million, including $12.0 million located outside of the United States, and $2.7 million that is subject to certain local regulations on repatriation.
audit_findings.explanation: Adding the entire cash balance is demonstrated, but treating it as excess is not demonstrated to be wrong because the required operating reserve and accessibility of foreign cash are absent. The full amount is large enough relative to scenario equity values to make the classification materially relevant.
audit_findings.action: Document March 2026 cash by entity and jurisdiction, legal restrictions and repatriation costs; estimate minimum liquidity from payroll, working-capital seasonality and committed facilities; then rerun the bridge using only distributable excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Defined-benefit liability is absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.0 million at June 30, 2025, about $0.12 per share and 0.8%-1.0% of scenario equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: An unfunded obligation not otherwise reflected in forecast owner earnings would be deducted as a claim ahead of common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: As of June 30, 2025 and 2024, defined benefit obligations of $ 2.0 million and $ 1.3 million, respectively, were included in other non-current liabilities in the consolidated balance sheets, and amounts recognized in net income for the years ended June 30, 2025, 2024, and 2023 were $ 0.3 million, $ 0.3 million, and $ 0.4 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The absence from the bridge is demonstrated, although whether future settlement cash flows are already embedded in owner earnings remains unresolved. Even a full $2.0 million deduction is only about $0.12 per share, versus values of $11.94-$16.25 and a $39.17 market price, so it cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Verify the March 2026 funded status and projected contribution treatment; if not embedded in owner earnings, deduct the current net underfunded amount in a consistency rerun.

audit_findings.title: The Lake Ball stake may be counted both in earnings and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $0.4 million bridge item; FY2025 share of profit was $1.116 million, equal to 7.5% of the $14.9 million anchor, with $1.093 million of distributions; total valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-method profit retained in historical owner earnings raises the OE anchor and its capitalized forecast, while separately adding the investment value duplicates the same economic claim.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s investment of $ 0.4 million at June 30, 2025 and 2024, respectively, is included in other non-current assets in the consolidated balance sheets, while net earnings from the joint venture is included in selling, general, and administrative expense in the consolidated statements of comprehensive income.
audit_findings.explanation: Double counting is not demonstrated because the owner-earnings workpapers do not show whether Lake Ball profit was purged. The $0.4 million bridge addition alone is immaterial, but the filed FY2025 profit equals 7.5% of anchor owner earnings and could propagate through operating and terminal value, making the unresolved treatment reasonably capable of materially affecting the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Trace Lake Ball profit and distributions through every historical OE calculation; either purge the investment's earnings before retaining the $0.4 million bridge asset or remove the bridge addition, then recompute the trend anchor and all scenarios.
